title: Fix 7 Bucks logo reliability + add PWA install prompt

requirements.summary: Fix logo asset path and implement a graceful fallback so the logo never shows a broken image placeholder on login or in the authenticated header.
acceptanceCriteria: On the login screen, the logo renders (no broken image icon) and uses the correct static asset path that is included in the production build.
In the authenticated header, the logo renders (no broken image icon) and uses the same correct static asset path included in the production build.
If the logo image fails to load for any reason, the UI shows a non-broken fallback (e.g., a styled '7 Bucks' wordmark block) instead of the browser broken-image placeholder.
No backend changes are required for the logo to display.

file_operations.description: Add a production-bundled, stable logo asset in the public folder (static file served at a consistent path) to replace the currently unreliable logo reference.

Create a reusable BrandLogo component that renders the shared logo from a single static path and provides an onError-driven fallback UI (styled text/wordmark block) to prevent broken-image placeholders.
Replace the inline logo with the shared BrandLogo component (same asset path as the header) so the login screen logo reliably loads and falls back gracefully if it cannot be loaded.
Replace the inline logo with the shared BrandLogo component so the authenticated header uses the same correct static asset path and shows a graceful fallback if the image fails.

requirements.summary: Configure the app as a PWA (manifest + icons + service worker) and add an in-app install button that appears only when install is supported, available on both login and authenticated views.
acceptanceCriteria: The app includes a valid web app manifest linked from the HTML entry point, with correct name/short_name, start_url, display mode, theme/background colors, and icon entries that match existing generated icon filenames.
A service worker is registered so the app is recognized as installable by supported browsers (where applicable in the build environment).

An install UI control with English text (e.g., "Install app") is shown only when the browser exposes an install prompt event / install capability; it is hidden otherwise (including on unsupported platforms such as iOS Safari).
Clicking the install control triggers the browser’s native install prompt when available, and the UI updates appropriately after the user accepts or dismisses the prompt.
The install prompt is available from the login screen (unauthenticated) and remains accessible in authenticated views (e.g., in the header or a consistent location).

file_operations.description: Add a valid PWA manifest (name/short_name/start_url/display/theme/background) referencing existing icon assets at frontend/public/assets/generated/seven-bucks-app-icon.dim_512x512.png and frontend/public/assets/generated/seven-bucks-favicon.dim_64x64.png.
Link the PWA manifest from the HTML entry point and ensure required PWA meta (e.g., theme color) is present so supported browsers recognize the app as installable.
Add a minimal service worker file under public so it can be registered by the app and meet installability expectations in supported environments (no push/analytics).
Create a small helper to register the service worker (guarded by feature detection) without modifying immutable entrypoint files.

Implement a hook that listens for install capability (e.g., beforeinstallprompt when available), exposes installability state, triggers the native prompt on click, and updates state after accept/dismiss; hide on unsupported platforms.

Create a reusable install UI control with English text (e.g., "Install app") that is only rendered when the hook indicates installation is supported and a prompt can be shown; handle post-action UI state.
Wire the PwaInstallButton into the login screen layout so the install experience is available while unauthenticated, and remains hidden when unsupported.
Wire the PwaInstallButton into the authenticated header (consistent location) so the install experience remains accessible after login, while still only showing when supported.
Register the service worker via the new helper in a top-level effect (without touching immutable files) so the app is recognized as a PWA where applicable.
